title: Access request jurisdictional routing and approval fabric
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We continue to get a mix of customer requests for admin changes that cross multiple organizational boundaries and legal jurisdictions (e.g., EU tenant requests, cross-tenant SAML changes, and SCIM provisioning toggles for partners). Current intake funnels everything into a single queue which increases lead time, creates manual context-switching for operators, and risks incorrect approvals for regionally restricted roles.

Problem statement: Without deterministic routing and an approval fabric that encodes jurisdictional policy, we see 48-72 hour SLAs miss rates for enterprise admin requests, increased risk of improper privilege grants, and repeated follow-ups from Sales/Customer Success. We need an automated intake-to-approval pipeline that classifies requests, scores risk, routes to the correct reviewer/workflow, and tracks SLA progress.

Goals:
- Reduce median time-to-resolution for enterprise admin requests from ~60h to <=24h for low-risk, <=48h for medium-risk, <=72h for high-risk (target SLAs).
- Eliminate jurisdictional policy violations by codifying regional gates (data residency, legal review) into routing.
- Make routing auditable and reversible (full trail stored in audit log).
- Provide clear UX for CS/engineers to self-serve low-risk tasks (e.g., read-only role grants) while surfacing high-risk escalation.

Scope: RBAC changes, SSO/SAML configuration changes, SCIM provisioning toggles, org policy exceptions (encryption/KMS access, cross-tenant linking). Excludes incident-driven emergency access (handled by separate on-call runbook).

Proposed solution: "Jurisdictional Routing & Approval Fabric" consisting of: 
1) Structured intake form: enforce required fields (tenant region, requested role/change type, justification, requested SLA, requester role, related GitHub/Confluence artifact). Add hinting to reduce incomplete requests.
2) Scoring engine: rule- + ML-hybrid that assigns risk band (low/medium/high) using signals: role sensitivity mapping, number of org-level scopes requested, tenant data residency, historical requester behavior, presence of external partner links.
3) Routing matrix: map (region, risk band, change type) -> review workflow: auto-approve (low), CS + operator review (medium), legal+security+product review (high). Include timeboxes/SLA counters.
4) Policy gates: codify jurisdictional constraints (e.g., EU tenants require DPA confirmation; US tenants with federal compliance tags require security review).
5) Approval fabric: record flows in our audit store, support delegated approvals (regional admins), and expose rollback buttons for operators.
6) Self-serve templates and CLI tooling for common safe actions (role read-only grants under specific conditions).
7) Observability: dashboard with queue sizes by routing lane, SLA burn-down, median resolution times, and top failure modes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Structured intake form live and validated in console and intake API.
- Routing matrix implemented and test cases for each (region x risk x change type) mapped.
- Audit events emitted for each state transition.
- Dashboard showing SLA compliance by lane with historical 90-day view.
- Runbook for operators and CS documented and reviewed.

Metrics:
- Median time-to-resolution by risk band (target: low <=24h, med <=48h, high <=72h).
- SLA hit rate > 90% for low and medium lanes within 30 days of rollout.
- Reduction in manual reassigns / cross-team escalations by 50%.

Design and UX notes: For mobile and console flows the intake should be a single progressive form; show routing hints to the requester ("Your request will be auto-approved" or "This will require legal review"). Provide a minimal view for CS to surface required attachments.

Security & legal: We flagged this for jurisdictional review. Legal needs an attachable DPA confirmation artifact for EU/regulatory tenants. Security review required for any grant giving KMS/HSM or super-admin grants.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict rules reduce manual work but may increase false positives causing over-escalation (temporary mitigation: allow operators to reclassify with reason logged).
- Conservative routing increases time for some requests; mitigated with self-serve templates for common safe operations.
- ML scoring deferred to phase 2 to avoid initial calibration risks; phase 1 uses deterministic rules with telemetry for later ML training.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (pilot): deterministic routing + intake form behind feature flag for 2 large customers run by Solutions Eng.
- Phase 1: expand to all enterprise tenants, add dashboards and operator runbook.
- Phase 2: ML risk scorer, automated auto-approve expansion, CLI self-serve templates.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/PM-46290+-+Jurisdictional+Routing+and+Approval+Fabric, intake form mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-example, initial backend schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4187, dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ae3-admin-routing

Open questions:
- Who are the canonical regional approvers for APAC (engineering or regional account leads)? (action: sync with Sales Ops).
- How do we encode partner-managed SCIM providers that have their own approval policies? (action: design workshop with Integrations team).

Next steps:
- Product to sign PRD -> PM review with Security & Legal (target 2026-03-15).
- ENG to estimate implementation tasks and unblock dependencies ENG-20412 (audit pipeline) and ENG-20987 (intake API).
- Design deliver intake form and accessible hints (deadline 2026-03-05).
